title: node-swapfile-scheduler-backpressure-wip
body:
TL;DR: One node in us-west-2a started using a swapfile created by a third-party monitoring agent during an intermittent disk pressure window. Kernel-level swapping + kubelet memory-eviction heuristics interacted badly, causing kubelet to declare Docker runtime unhealthy and trigger mass pod restarts. The scheduler then experienced backpressure (many pending pods, bursty binds) which increased API server pressure and prolonged recovery. This doc captures our timeline, immediate mitigations, root-cause hypothesis, short-term runbook edits, and follow-ups.

Summary of incident
- Impact: ~12 pods across 4 deployments repeatedly restarted over a 27-minute window (11:08–11:35 UTC). Some user-facing endpoints saw 5xx spikes (5m p95 latency doubled).
- Affected zone: us-west-2a, node pool: gpu-preemptible-medium. Other zones healthy.
- Likely trigger: swapfile created/enabled on node by monitoring agent update; swap activity + background GC led to memory.available drop below eviction threshold.

Why this is different from typical OOM events
- Not a pure OOM killer case. kernel did not kill app processes first; instead system started swapping and page reclaim slowed application, causing kubelet liveness probes to fail and CRI restart cycles.
- Kubelet's eviction logic uses memory.available and ephemeral-storage; because swap was present, memory.available readings were misleading for the node's real working set. The node oscillated between "MemoryPressure" and healthy repeatedly.

Immediate timeline (collected from node logs, kube-apiserver events, and pod lifecycle):
- 11:04 UTC: monitoring-agent (v2.3.1) rollout to node triggered. Agent applied a local swapfile creation as fallback for low-memory host scenarios (new feature flag).
- 11:07 UTC: kernel begins swapping; dmesg shows high swap-in/out rates and page reclaim spikes.
- 11:08 UTC: kubelet records MemoryPressure conditions intermittently; eviction manager attempts to evict a few best-effort pods.
- 11:10 UTC: CRI runtime (containerd) starts restarting containers deemed unresponsive; kubelet marks node NotReady for short windows due to probe timeouts.
- 11:12 UTC: Scheduler sees surge of pending pods for node-affine workloads; cluster-autoscaler not triggered because node still present and under pressure.
- 11:25 UTC: oncall manually drained node; created cordon and drain to stop pod churn while we investigated.
- 11:35 UTC: node recovered after disabling swap and restarting kubelet; pods gradually rescheduled elsewhere or restarted successfully.

Key logs/metrics collected (pull these next when doing a deeper postmortem):
- dmesg excerpt around 11:07–11:15 (swap-in/out counts, page reclaim times)
- /var/log/kubelet.log evictions, eviction manager thresholds, and outbound API server errors
- containerd/cri logs showing liveness probe failures and restart reasons
- node-level vmstat and free output to show memory & swap activity
- kube-apiserver request latencies (spike correlation with bind/attach events)

Immediate mitigations taken during incident
- 11:16 UTC: cordon node-abc123 to prevent new pods assigning
- 11:18 UTC: temporary taint application to keep critical pods from moving
- 11:20 UTC: disabled monitoring-agent feature flag remotely where possible
- 11:23 UTC: removed swapfile (sudo swapoff -a; rm /swapfile) and restarted kubelet (systemctl restart kubelet)
- 11:28 UTC: rebalanced a few critical deployments to healthy nodes to reduce API server pressure

Why "disable swap" fixed it (quick note)
- Kubernetes expects swap to be off or kubelet to be configured with --fail-swap-on=false (rare). Swap introduces unpredictability in memory.available metrics and can break eviction heuristics; disabling returned memory metrics to expected behavior and prevented kubelet from oscillating between evicting/resurrecting pods.

Short-term runbook edits (draft)
- Add a preflight check on node image/agent packaging: ensure no swapfile is created by default. Document explicit opt-in and require infra-review for agents that manipulate vm settings.
- Update SRE incident runbook: "If you see swap activity + MemoryPressure in kubelet: cordon node, disable swap, restart kubelet, monitor evictions for 10 min." (include exact commands and verification steps)
  - commands to include: sudo swapon --show; free -h; vmstat 1 10; sudo swapoff -a; systemctl restart kubelet; kubectl get nodes -o wide; kubectl describe node <node> | grep -i eviction -A3
- Add alerting rule: Detect swap presence on nodes and fire a P1 if swap.active on >1% of nodes in a pool. (Prometheus node_exporter metric: node_memory_SwapTotal_bytes > 0 or custom node_swap_active gauge)
- Add gating to cluster-autoscaler: if node shows MemoryPressure events repeatedly, consider transient scaling logic (invest more later).

Open questions / unresolved
- How did the monitoring agent decide to create swapfile? Feature flag misconfiguration or new default on that build? Need to trace deploy pipeline for agent v2.3.1.
- Why did containerd/kubelet not reconcile quicker? Was the liveness probe timeout conservative? Are we seeing probe timeouts due to page reclaim CPU contention?
- Why cluster-autoscaler did not relieve pressure by spinning up replacement nodes? Autoscaler logic ignores nodes that are NotReady transiently; consider tuning or manual trigger thresholds.
- Could we detect this class of incident earlier by combining swap detection + rising page faults and kubelet MemoryPressure events?

Short checklist for the postmortem (owner: Marisol)
- [ ] Pull full dmesg and vmstat outputs from node-abc123 (Devon)
- [ ] Capture exact agent rollout timeline (Priya)
- [ ] Reproduce on a staging node (with swap) to verify behavior and kubelet eviction interactions (Liam)
- [ ] Draft a short agent packaging policy to prevent swap creation (Marisol)
- [ ] Implement prom alert for swap presence (SRE infra)
- [ ] Update runbook and push to Confluence + link from k8s incident playbook (Marisol)

Mitigation proposals (short term vs long term)
- Short term: Add detection and alert for swap presence; block agent rollouts that create swap through CI checks; require QA signoff in canaries.
- Medium term: Harden kubelet eviction thresholds to be less sensitive to transient swap usage and add backoff windows for evictions triggered in quick succession. Evaluate kube-reserved and eviction-hard defaults across node-pools.
- Long term: Add a preflight validator in our node bootstrap that asserts swap is off and that agents cannot create swapfiles without a signed opt-in. Make this part of image-scan policy in infra repo.

Notes to reviewers
- This is a working doc; I expect to add attach logs and exact command outputs before closing. Please add Slack links or screenshots to linked_artifacts if you have them. If you were oncall, jot quick notes here about what you tried and any commands you ran.

Appendix: useful commands (copy-paste friendly)
- Check swap: sudo swapon --show || echo "no swap"
- Show memory & swap usage: free -h && vmstat 1 5
- Disable swap: sudo swapoff -a && sudo rm -f /swapfile
- Restart kubelet: sudo systemctl restart kubelet
- Cordon node: kubectl cordon <node>
- Drain node safely: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- Describe evictions/events: kubectl describe node <node> | sed -n '/Events:/,${p}' | sed -n '1,50p'

End of draft.
